tasks.title: Fix the macOS dual-runtime handle mismatch
acceptanceCriteria: load_duckdb() never leaves two libduckdb runtimes loaded RTLD_GLOBAL: when the wheel lacks C-API symbols, both the Python duckdb module and numbduck bind duckdb_* to the single standalone library.
extract_connection_ptr detects the dual-runtime condition and raises a clear RuntimeError instead of passing a Connection* across runtime boundaries.
A test (skipif not macOS / not a C-API-stripped wheel) asserts that on the fallback configuration either a single runtime is used or pybridge refuses with RuntimeError.
flake8 --max-line-length=120 clean.
tasks.rationale: On macOS with a C-API-stripped wheel the loader keeps the wheel runtime loaded and adds a second standalone runtime; pybridge can then mix handles across them (undefined behavior). Coordinate with the version-match work in T5 (XC-ver-2).

tasks.title: Runtime duckdb version/layout guard and graceful failure in pybridge
acceptanceCriteria: extract_connection_ptr reads duckdb.__version__ and refuses (RuntimeError) on a (version, platform, C++ runtime) combination not in a validated set; offsets come from a single per-version table, not bare literals.
NULL/None intermediate pointers (cpp_obj_p, conn_ptr) raise the documented RuntimeError before any dereference.
A test asserts a closed/garbage connection yields RuntimeError rather than a segfault or TypeError, and an unsupported duckdb version triggers the version guard.
flake8 --max-line-length=120 clean.
tasks.rationale: The +16/+32 offsets are validated only on duckdb 1.3.2 / Linux / libstdc++ but the supported range is 1.3.2-1.5.x across platforms; without a version gate and NULL guards, layout drift silently yields a wrong pointer or segfaults.

tasks.title: CI matrix: add macOS, fix benchmark deselection, widen Windows
acceptanceCriteria: numbduck_ci.yml includes at least one macos-latest (ARM64) job that runs load_duckdb end-to-end (e.g. via NUMBDUCK_LIBDUCKDB pointing at a brew libduckdb) and the job is green.

Benchmarks are deselected in CI: pyproject.toml sets addopts = "-m 'not benchmark'" (or the CI pytest step uses -m 'not benchmark') and the marker description matches; a CI run shows test_udf_benchmark deselected.
A Windows job at the duckdb floor (1.3.2) is added, or the narrowed Windows coverage is documented in a workflow comment.
The full CI matrix is green.
tasks.rationale: macOS (the project's hardest loader path) has zero CI coverage, the benchmark marker is never actually deselected so the 1M-row benchmark runs every job, and Windows ABI coverage is one thin slice.

tasks.title: Rewrite stale CLAUDE.md to match origin/main
acceptanceCriteria: CLAUDE.md no longer references nonexistent ducklib helpers (_call_lib_func_struct_in/out, _emit_byval_call, _build_packed_interval) or 'custom @intrinsic' codegen; it states decimal/varint/interval route through numbox's _call_lib_func.
The stale 'Follow-ups' migration section and the ducklib.py:1525-1640 / :298-433 line references are removed.
The numbox pin in CLAUDE.md reads numbox~=0.5.11 (matching pyproject.toml).
'Adding a New Binding' step 1 no longer contradicts step 5 on docstring link targets.
No CLAUDE.md line reference points past the EOF of the file it cites.
tasks.rationale: Multiple CLAUDE.md sections describe an already-completed migration and helpers/intrinsics that do not exist, and misstate the numbox floor, misleading future contributors.

tasks.title: Verify integrity of the downloaded/cached libduckdb and confirm version match
acceptanceCriteria: _download_libduckdb verifies the downloaded bytes against a pinned per-version SHA-256 before extracting/loading and refuses on mismatch; NUMBDUCK_LIBDUCKDB_DOWNLOAD=1 does not bypass the digest check.
_find_standalone_libduckdb re-verifies the pinned digest on every cache hit; the cache dir is created mode=0o700 and the file is written via a temp file + os.replace.
After loading a standalone/Homebrew/env library, the loaded version is checked (duckdb_library_version) against duckdb.__version__ and a mismatch warns or raises.
The CI install pins numbox to an exact version (or a hash-pinned constraints file) so builds are reproducible.
A test asserts a tampered/wrong-digest cached dylib is rejected.
tasks.rationale: The macOS download/cache path dlopens unverified native code RTLD_GLOBAL (arbitrary code execution surface) and never checks that a standalone/Homebrew library matches the wheel's version.

tasks.title: Harden pybridge input validation
acceptanceCriteria: The type guard uses exact-type identity (type(conn) is duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection); a test asserts an isinstance-spoofing object is rejected with TypeError before any pointer read.
A closed connection is rejected with the documented RuntimeError (not a TypeError, None return, or segfault); a test exercises conn.close() then extract_connection_ptr.
Every NULL/None intermediate read raises the documented RuntimeError; no failure mode escapes the documented TypeError/RuntimeError contract.
The docstring states the SELECT 1 step is best-effort and does not guarantee memory safety.
flake8 --max-line-length=120 clean.
tasks.rationale: The lone isinstance guard is spoofable and there is no closed-connection or NULL-pointer handling, so crafted/closed connections drive arbitrary memory reads or contract-violating exceptions.

tasks.title: Fix idx_t signedness and vector_get_validity pointer typing
acceptanceCriteria: All idx_t returns/args (ducklib.py:105,155,156,157,225,233) are typed uint64, matching the rest of the file and duckdb.h.
duckdb_vector_get_validity is typed intp(intp), matching duckdb_vector_get_data and the validity arg of duckdb_validity_row_is_valid.
A test calls duckdb_vector_get_validity and feeds the result into duckdb_validity_row_is_valid inside @njit with no uint64->int64 coercion.
pytest green; flake8 --max-line-length=120 clean.
tasks.rationale: Six idx_t entries are signed intp instead of uint64 and the validity pointer is mistyped as a uint64 scalar, breaking the all-pointers-are-intp convention and risking numba int/uint -> float64 unification.

tasks.title: Harden CI workflows (script injection, numbox pin, action SHAs)
acceptanceCriteria: No github.* context value is interpolated directly into a run: script; github.ref_name is passed via an env: block, referenced as a quoted shell variable, and validated against a strict regex before being written to __init__.py.
numbox is pinned to an explicit version in the CI install (mirroring numba/duckdb) in both numbduck_ci.yml and haversine_bench.yml.
All action references are pinned to full 40-char commit SHAs with a version comment, including the third-party lychee-action.
CI is green after the changes.
tasks.rationale: The version step splices github.ref_name into a shell script and into __init__.py (latent RCE/injection), numbox is left floating, and actions are pinned to mutable tags.

tasks.title: Fix the empty committed __version__
acceptanceCriteria: numbduck/__init__.py carries a valid PEP 440 fallback version (e.g. 0.0.0.dev0) or version resolution moves to setuptools-scm.
A local `python -m build` produces a wheel with a non-empty, PEP 440-valid version without the CI overwrite step.
CI version injection (tag / run-number path) still works.
tasks.rationale: The committed __version__ = "" makes local builds silently produce an empty/invalid version; only CI's overwrite step yields a real version.

tasks.title: Fix DuckDB handle leaks in tests and add leak guards
acceptanceCriteria: test_query, the column/row-count test, and the five aux_get_data_vector consumers call duckdb_destroy_result / duckdb_destroy_data_chunk before tearing down the DB.
A C-handle balance check (or a re-destroy-of-zeroed-handle no-op assertion) guards at least one result/chunk lifecycle so a missing-destroy regression fails the suite.
pytest green; no test leaks a result or chunk.
tasks.rationale: Several tests leak duckdb_result/data_chunk handles and the C-handle side has no leak accounting (unlike the NRT side), so missing-destroy or double-free regressions pass silently.

tasks.title: Add a @cfunc UDAF exception guard
acceptanceCriteria: Each callback impl (init/update/combine/finalize/destroy) wraps its body in a bare try/except (not try/finally), releasing/decrefing any borrowed structref and signalling failure on the error path.
A test induces a raise inside update/combine (e.g. a forced allocation failure or bad input) and asserts NRT alloc==free afterward (no MemInfo leak).
irr.main's alloc==free leak gate still passes.
tasks.rationale: A raise inside a callback impl is swallowed by @cfunc, skipping the borrowed-state decref (MemInfo leak) and returning a silently wrong aggregate.

tasks.title: Fix irr convergence tolerance and bracket
acceptanceCriteria: irr_bisect converges on bracket width in r and returns (r_lo+r_hi)/2 once converged (not NaN); a test with large-magnitude cashflows (e.g. scaled x100) asserts a finite, correct IRR rather than NaN.
The no-sign-change / out-of-bracket case is distinguishable from the documented empty-group NaN.
Existing irr tests still pass.
tasks.rationale: The absolute NPV convergence gate cannot be met for realistic (large) cashflow magnitudes, so a converged root returns NaN indistinguishable from an empty group; the fixed bracket has the same NaN-conflation issue.

tasks.title: Guard the legacy-cache os.remove and fix library preference
acceptanceCriteria: The legacy-cache os.remove is wrapped in try/except OSError (or moved after a library is located) so an un-removable stale file never aborts loading; a test simulates a failing remove and asserts loading proceeds.
find_duckdb_shared_lib selects version-aware (1.4+ _duckdb* preferred on 1.4+), anchors its regexes, and resolves multiple matches deterministically.
flake8 --max-line-length=120 clean.
tasks.rationale: An unguarded os.remove aborts loading even when a valid library exists, and the 1.3-first / strict-singleton lookup can pick the wrong library or raise on transitional layouts.

tasks.title: Fix stale line cites and links in the design doc
acceptanceCriteria: Every test_ducklib.py line/anchor cited in test_ducklib.md resolves to the function/block it describes (Welford callbacks ~L3273-L3375, registration ~L3477-L3500, refcount-ladder test L2999, commented intrinsic ~L2882-L2919).
doc-codeblock-flake8 and link-check CI pass.
tasks.rationale: Four cites point at unrelated code, breaking the design doc's traceability into the implementation.

tasks.title: Reorganize the orphaned bind/scalar wrappers at EOF
acceptanceCriteria: The four EOF bind wrappers (hugeint/uhugeint/interval/decimal) sit with the bind_* run and the two scalar wrappers with the scalar block; the trailing sig keys move into the scalar sig block.
pytest green (no binding lost or duplicated); flake8 --max-line-length=120 clean.
tasks.rationale: Migration residue left six wrappers appended at EOF, so the dict order and wrapper order disagree and the bind family looks incomplete.

tasks.title: Close test coverage gaps
acceptanceCriteria: A multi-chunk test selects >2048 rows, loops duckdb_fetch_chunk until null, and asserts row totals and values spanning a chunk boundary.
A DECIMAL(38,x) test reads the column back as a 16-byte int128 (both halves) and a get_decimal round-trip exceeds 2**63.
test_struct_size_guard either drives a >16B struct round-trip or is renamed to reflect it tests tuple arithmetic only.
Added value assertions: create_array_value elements, get_value_type type id, create_get_bit payload bytes, combined Welford .mean; invalid-param-index covered for the struct binds.
aux_read_inline_string documents or branches on the <=12-byte inline-string precondition.
pytest green.
tasks.rationale: Multiple tests assert existence but not value, multi-chunk and high-precision decimal paths are untested, and the inline-string reader has an implicit length<=12 precondition.

tasks.title: Harden the example UDF patterns
acceptanceCriteria: online_scoring checks the duckdb_state of bind/execute, guards chunk_p != 0 before reading vectors, and destroys the prepared statement via try/finally.

haversine and fraud_score either document the non-NULL input precondition inline or fetch validity masks; the builder handle is destroyed on the register-failure path (try/finally or destroy-before-assert).
irr's leak test forces the combine path (parallel aggregation / larger table) inside the alloc==free guarded region.
All examples still run and their cross-checks pass.
tasks.rationale: The reference examples omit return-code/NULL-chunk/validity checks and leak handles on error paths, and the irr leak guard never exercises the combine path where the subtlest hazards live.

tasks.title: Fix the example test helpers
acceptanceCriteria: format_table raises ValueError when a row's cell count != header count; a test covers the mismatch.
assert_results_match treats both-NaN as equal and documents scalar-only support (or uses numpy.array_equal(equal_nan=True)).
flake8 --max-line-length=120 clean.
tasks.rationale: format_table never validates row length (IndexError or silent truncation) and the cross-check spuriously fails on identical NaN results.

tasks.title: ducklib cleanup (dead code, ordering, name SoT, docstring URLs)
acceptanceCriteria: Dead code removed: _is_win and the now-unused import sys.
duckdb_connect moved to its sorted slot so the dict and wrapper order are consistent.
The two varint docstring URLs are normalized to the canonical https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/clients/c/api.html#... form.
A test asserts, for every wrapper, that the _call_lib_func string literal and the docstring anchor match the def name and a registered signature key.
pytest green; flake8 --max-line-length=120 clean; link-check CI passes.
tasks.rationale: ducklib carries dead Windows code, an out-of-order key, two non-canonical varint URLs, and an un-checked name copy (the docstring anchor) that lets DCK-sig-DES-4 happen.

tasks.title: utils refactor (path constants, decompose download, error guidance, version coupling)
acceptanceCriteria: The cached-dylib filename and path are single module constants used by both producer and consumer.
_download_libduckdb is split into a consent-policy function and a _fetch_and_cache(url, dest) that is unit-testable with a file:// URL and a tmp dest.
The legacy-cache cleanup is moved out of the locator (or Darwin-gated) and the os.remove guarded.

Download/extract failures and the non-Darwin missing-library case raise a RuntimeError carrying brew/NUMBDUCK_LIBDUCKDB guidance and the attempted URL/path; the version string is normalized before forming the release tag.
A unit test drives _fetch_and_cache against a local file:// archive; flake8 --max-line-length=120 clean.
tasks.rationale: utils duplicates the cache filename, bundles consent/fetch/unzip/write into one untestable function, mutates the filesystem from a locator, and surfaces bare HTTPError/KeyError with no guidance on version skew.

tasks.title: pybridge polish (named offsets, error context, docstring, lifetime note)
acceptanceCriteria: The 16/32 offsets are named module constants with the derivation comment attached.
The validation RuntimeError message includes duckdb.__version__ and a re-verify hint.
The docstring describes the SELECT 1 step as best-effort (not offset validation) and documents the borrowed-pointer lifetime contract (caller must keep conn alive and open).
flake8 --max-line-length=120 clean; pytest green.
tasks.rationale: Offsets are bare literals, the failure message lacks context, the docstring overstates the validation, and the borrowed pointer escapes with no documented lifetime coupling.

tasks.title: Make version-gated bindings raise clearly for JIT callers
acceptanceCriteria: Calling a version-gated binding absent from the loaded libduckdb from @njit raises a clear, named error at typing time instead of an opaque TypingError (via an @njit-introspectable stub or a Python-level capability check before compiling dependent JIT code).
A test (skipif the symbol is present) asserts the clear error.
If the root fix lands in numbox, an upstream follow-up is referenced; pytest green.
tasks.rationale: @cres_if_available stubs raise NotImplementedError only for Python callers; from @njit (the intended consumer) they surface an opaque TypingError.

tasks.title: Document/guard the duckdb_utils dangling-pointer footgun
acceptanceCriteria: Each allocator's docstring states that the returned array (not the extracted handle int) must outlive all DuckDB use of its .ctypes.data.
flake8 --max-line-length=120 clean.
tasks.rationale: The allocators return bare ndarrays with no coupling to the handle DuckDB writes, so `p = create_duckdb_result().ctypes.data` dangles when the temporary is collected; latent today but worth documenting.
